messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multi_normal caused segmentation fault
parts:
Taking this over to stan-dev now...

So I'm not sure I follow the pattern with the nested memory stuff, but here is what happens:

- initialize_state_random first calls stan::model::gradient() which calls stan::agrad::gradient() which evaluates the gradient but cleans up with stan::agrad::recover_memory_nested()
- recover_memory_nested() calls delete on the elements of var_alloc_stack_ but doesn't clear it so var_alloc_stack now has some defunct pointers in it.
- the optimizer then calls stan::model::log_prob_grad() which evaluates the gradient and cleans up with stan::agrad::recover_memory() which, at this point tries to delete defunct pointers on var_alloc_stack_.

My hunch is that var_alloc_stack_ needs to be cleared (or truncated) in recover_memory_nested(), but I don't understand the nested memory stuff so I didn't want to just dive in.

Cheers,
Marcus


On Thu, Jan 8, 2015 at 1:31 PM, Marcus Brubaker <marcus.a...@gmail.com> wrote:
A chainable_alloc (LDLT_alloc in particular) is ending up on the var_alloc_stack twice for some reason, not at all sure why though.  The crash arises due to a double delete.  My current theory is that somewhere var_alloc_stack is not getting clear()d in the optimizers calling pattern, otherwise it should show up during sampling but I'm not sure where or how.

Cheers,
Marcus


On Thu, Jan 8, 2015 at 1:00 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
I think there's an issue somewhere in the optimization code
that we're trying to track down before the 2.6 release, which
should be soon.

An unrelated comment:  If you have variables with fixed values,
as in cov and k here, it's better to define them in the transformed
data block for efficiency.  Making them local variables in the model
turns them into parameter-like variables and derivatives of the log
prob with respect to them get calculated but are never needed.

- Bob

> On Jan 8, 2015, at 11:00 AM, He-chien Tsai <depo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm using cmdstan. When I optimize the model. After showing configurations, it shows only one line error "Segmentation fault (core dumped)"
> At the same time, sampling is accomplish without any problem.
> My original model is complicated so I replace it with belows which shows actually the same error:
>
> parameters{
>   vector[2] a;
> }
>
> model{
>   matrix[2,2] cov;
>   vector[2] k;
>   k[1] <- 0;
>   k[2] <- 0;
>   cov[1,1] <- 1;
>   cov[1,2] <- 0.5;
>   cov[2,1] <- 0.5;
>   cov[2,2] <- 1;
>   a ~ multi_normal(k, cov);
> }
>
> Any suggestion?
>

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] multi_normal caused segmentation fault
parts:
Thanks --- I should be able to fix it from here.

The nested memory is used for the ODE solver in order to evaluate
system sensitivities to create the coupled system to plug into the
integrator.

The basic pattern is to mark where you're at on the stacks, do a
gradient calc just on the top of the stack, and then
recover back down to marks when the nested gradient's calculated.
It looks like I missed one of the recovers.

- Bob
